items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to providing for direct private assistance to emerging technology companies through the trading of their existing but unused research and development credits and their existing but unused net operating loss deductions to existing corporations and partnerships in return for private assistance
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4228

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the tax law, in relation to providing for direct private
assistance to emerging technology companies through the trading of their
existing but unused research and development credits and their existing
but unused net operating loss deductions to existing corporations and
partnerships in return for private assistance

PURPOSE OF THE BILL:
To authorize the trading of existing unused
research and development credits and existing but unused net
operating loss deductions to existing entities. This bill establishes
a corporation business tax benefit certificate transfer program to
allow new or expanding small high technology companies in New York to
surrender its unused amounts of research and development tax credits
and unused net operating loss carryover to other corporations in
exchange for private financial assistance.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
§ 1- Creates the "Small New York Based
High-Technology Business Investment Tax Credit Act."

§ 2- Creates a new § 212 to the Tax Law, which authorizes the Tax
Department to develop a corporation business tax benefit certificate
transfer program. The Commissioner, in cooperation with the
Commissioner of the Department of Economic Development would review
and approve applications by new or expanding emerging technology and
biotechnology companies in this state with unused but otherwise
allowable carryover of research and development tax credits pursuant
to § 210 subdivision 12(b) (i) of the Tax Law, and otherwise
allowable net operating loss carryovers pursuant to . 208 subdivision
9(f) of the Tax Law, to surrender those tax benefits in exchange for
private financial assistance to be made a corporation filing pursuant
to Article 9A of the tax law, who has obtained a corporation business
tax benefit certificate in an amount equal to at least 75% of the
amount of the surrendered tax benefits.

§ 3- Adds a new § 606-A to the Tax Law to provide for a similar
program but allows for surrender of research and development tax
credits pursuant to § 606 (a) (2) (A) of the Tax Law, and otherwise
allowable net operating loss carryovers pursuant § 617(b), and
633(b) of the Tax Law.

§ 4- Effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:
Emerging high-tech companies often find difficulty in
accessing the capital they require to grow and create high-value jobs.
Traditional bank financing does not meet their needs, and venture funds
are not always available at certain stages of development and in
various regions of the State.

These small firms often need numerous infusions of capital before they
become profitable. They are not able to take advantage of the net


operation loss, (NOL), deduction in the Tax Law, as without profits,
they have no tax liability. Allowing new, high-tech firms to sell
their NOLs to profitable companies provides a market-based solution
to their capital access problems, and benefits other firms in the
economy as well.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
2009-2010: A.2818
2007-2008: A.3022/S.2996
2005-2006: A.3525-A/S.1386-A
2003-2004: A.6147/S.2997
2001-2002: A.944/S.4210
1999-2000: A.7289-A/S.5680

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply
to taxable years which commence on or after January 1, 2011.
